purpose: Source-bound comparison of recovery/controller actions relevant to persistent self-improvement. Mechanism evidence from within-task recovery is kept separate from cross-task persistent evolution evidence.

systems.title: AgentRewind: Recoverable Execution for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
systems.scope_class: within-task long-horizon runtime recovery; not persistent cross-task self-improvement
controller_actions: Restart from root while carrying evaluator-derived failure experience
Resume ancestor via aligned context+environment rewind while carrying rewind memory
systems.matched_design: Experiments share agent/tools/environments, greedy decoding and termination conditions; paper also includes paired recovery from identical failed endpoints with rewind availability as the key difference.
systems.inference_within_scope: When a failure is suffix-local and earlier state remains useful, selective rollback that restores both environment and context while retaining failure knowledge can dominate clean restart and forward-only continuation.
limits: Controlled workspace/environment only; external irreversible side effects are outside the demonstrated rollback scope.
No official source repository was source-bound in this run, so crash atomicity and checkpoint implementation were not independently audited.
Do not generalize these task-recovery gains to persistent cross-task self-improvement without a matched persistent experiment.

systems.title: Fail-Fast, Restart-Smart: Early Failure Prediction and Restart for SWE Agentic Tasks
systems.scope_class: within-task SWE runtime recovery; not persistent cross-task self-improvement
controller_actions: Restart-with-artifact by offering interrupted repository diff as optional overlay
systems.inference_within_scope: Restarting need not discard all trajectory value; preserving a bounded artifact overlay can outperform cold restart when the interrupted trajectory contains useful code changes.
limits: This is a single-active-trajectory controller, not an evolving long-term agent memory policy.
False-positive setting changes the compute/success tradeoff; the 25% FP result is not a universal operating point.

systems.title: ScienceFlow: A long-horizon agent for ML research, scientific discovery and beyond
systems.scope_class: persistent long-horizon autoresearch with recoverable executable state
controller_actions: Process resume from persisted workspace/memory/tool cursor

public_resume_contract.task_level: reuse same workspace and account remaining budget from logs/state.json
public_resume_contract.agent_memory_level: reload persisted ScienceAgent history and decide next LLM round versus pending tool execution
public_resume_contract.tool_cursor_level: if exactly one assistant tool call is at the memory tail without a tool result, execute that tool directly, append its result, then continue
public_resume_contract.tested_behavior: Public unit tests verify detection of a single pending tool call, direct tool execution without re-logging the assistant message, transition back to continue_llm, resume monitor events, and heartbeat behavior during a resumed bash tool.

systems.inference_within_scope: Persistent autoresearch benefits from recoverable archived executable states and separate execution control under the tested 24h MLE-Lite budget. The public code also demonstrates concrete process-resume semantics at workspace, memory and single-tool-cursor levels.
limits: The ablation removes ESTRA as a whole and does not separately compare all four ESTRA action combinations.
The reported benchmark outcome is not a physically isolated outer lockbox for the adaptive research loop; retrospective test curves in the paper are analysis-only where described.
The inspected tests do not establish semantic equivalence under arbitrary crash points for every controller/evaluation state transition.

systems.title: FORGE: Self-Evolving Agent Memory With No Weight Updates via Population Broadcast
systems.key_boundary: Public resume path did not persist graduated_instances, so a process restart could reactivate and overwrite a lineage that uninterrupted execution had frozen.
systems.use_in_current_matrix: Contrasts with ScienceFlow's explicit persisted-memory/tool-cursor resume support and motivates separate durable artifact/controller/evaluation-consumption state.

synthesis.minimal_state_rewind_hypothesis: Prefer the smallest rollback/re-anchor that removes invalid causal dependencies while preserving independently validated prefix/artifacts and carrying explicit failure evidence. This is a synthesis hypothesis, not a theorem or a single-paper result.
durability_requirement: controller state including frozen/retired/active status, parent identity and budgets
evaluation-consumption state including evidence already used for selection and outer evidence still untouched
pending side-effect/tool cursor with replay/idempotency contract
synthesis.remaining_gap: No source-bound public real-LLM system found in this continuation directly compares at least three of Stop / Continue / Restart-clean / Restart-with-artifact / Resume-ancestor / Widen / Reopen under matched total proposal/evaluation budget, while also proving crash-equivalent controller state, candidate-local anytime-valid promotion, proposal-crossing durable statistical spending, immutable artifact identity, bounded selection feedback, complete proposal chronology, and a selection-unused outer test.

exact_next_action: Audit ScienceFlow's ESTRA Stage/anchor persistence and resume tests for whether archived-anchor identity, resource budgets, and stage/evaluation ledgers are reconstructed equivalently across kill points. Then search for a system with a true matched multi-action controller experiment (at least Continue, clean restart, artifact-preserving restart/rewind, and strategy redirect) under a common budget and unused outer test; prioritize crash-injection/restart-equivalence tests and complete action chronology.
